report:
The ruled-surface construction is mathematically established throughout 0<α<1 and c≥α, including references with infinite nonlinear first moment. I found no concrete mathematical defect in its stated scoped conclusions. The verdict concerns the original unrestricted S18 completion criteria: the argument explicitly leaves that direction and the general P14 bridge unresolved. Its results constitute substantive scoped progress.

I independently reconstructed the current source, supplement, historical proof within its original range, S11 companion, and notes n1–n7. Previous verdicts, candidate flags, computational observations, claimed source-reading records, and file hashes were not mathematical premises. The old S11 passages labelled urn:xean:task are not grants in the present task; their mathematical contents were checked against external primary sources. BEGZ, Bedford–Taylor, and BGL were opened directly. Direct retrieval of Demailly’s full book repeatedly timed out, but the matching author-hosted indexed passages for the necessary canonical, pullback, and removal results were recovered and inspected.

A. The imposed type and both small-curvature constructions are valid. With the stipulated dd^c normalization, the derivatives of χ give dd^cU≥−αw off p. Canonical removal retains this inequality and the value −∞ at p. The transverse logarithmic ratio and boundary flux tend to zero, so the curve current has no point atom. The estimate exp(tT^α)=exp(o(T)) proves integrability at every real weight and hence trivial ideals. An analytic singularity on a transverse disk is either bounded or has a positive logarithmic coefficient, excluding ordinary equivalence with U.

The piecewise χ_L is increasing, convex, and C¹ at −L. Its unchanged singular tail differs from U by a finite constant, its curvature loss ε_L tends to zero, and U≤U_L≤0 gives L¹ convergence to zero. The alternative q_L=L^α−(L−G_p)^α has the same ordinary type and loss αL^(α−1). Neither construction removes the pole. At c=α the original reference remains admissible; sufficiently small-curvature representatives also supply strict currents in its mutual ordinary type. Every application involving a small residual coefficient uses such a representative rather than assuming the original U is admissible there.

B. The entire rough competitor calculation is valid. For K=C(w₁+w₂) dominating θ, S=K+dd^cv and S₀=K+dd^cu are closed positive currents in the same Kähler class. Ordinary equivalence gives local boundedness outside the closed locally complete pluripolar divisor D. Thus comparison applies in both orders, in degrees one and two. All comparison hypotheses concern K, not the nonclosed background. Mutual comparison yields equal product classes; pointedness of the positive cone follows by pairing with a Kähler form. These are the precisely applicable hypotheses of [BEGZ Theorem 1.16](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~guedj/fichierspdf/BEGZ10.pdf).

The separated reference has first-current identity and square 2C(Cw₁+dd^cu)∧w₂, with full mass 2C² and no mass on D. Degree-one comparison gives zero K-trace for the positive defect S−⟨S⟩=1_DS. Strict positivity of K forces that defect to vanish. Degree-two comparison gives full closed square mass for every rough competitor. This establishes the needed absence of polar coefficient measures; it is not inferred merely from zero generic divisorial Lelong numbers.

Writing R=θ−K, bounded Bedford–Taylor locality outside D gives the polynomial expansion. Its terms ⟨S²⟩, 2R∧S, and R² are finite, assign D zero mass, and therefore identify the actual extended measure globally. Positivity follows from the bounded local smooth-background construction and zero mass on D. Distributional Stokes then gives M(v)=∫θ²+2∫v dd^cθ. The final pairing requires only L¹ integrability against a smooth density. No global unbounded multilinearity assertion or nonlinear first moment is needed.

Canonical averaging over the second sphere preserves both positivity and the affine mass functional. Its bounded inequalities against U survive canonical recovery, including the pole values. The resulting curve measure cw+dd^cq is positive with total mass c, proving 2c min a≤M(v)≤2c max a for every original competitor. The extremizing sequences are actual same-type potentials: their smooth positive measures provide a curvature margin, and L_j can simultaneously make ε_Lj and the smooth correction pairing sufficiently small. They concentrate at either extremum, including when that point is p. Equivalence constants may depend on j. Consequently both stated extrema are exact, positive, and finite.

C. Both all-test variational proofs are valid. The smooth Green kernel supplies the sphere Poisson solutions used in the construction. For H=∫(m/a)w and V=2c/H, the positive gauge representative Ω=gw₁+aw₂ satisfies Ω²=Vμ. Stokes applies to every smooth positive dd^c-closed test, and the matrix arithmetic–geometric mean inequality supplies the lower bound. The closed positive T=Ω/a attains it with numerator 2c and denominator √V H. Mixed and fiber-dependent tests are included.

Independently, the companion’s fiber-integral argument makes an arbitrary test’s averaged vertical coefficient a positive constant κ. With A its a-weighted horizontal integral, determinant positivity and Cauchy–Schwarz give D²≤2AκH, and (A−cκ)²≥0 gives the same bound. Thus neither proof silently restricts the test family. The historical note’s infimum of squared quotients agrees here with the stipulated square of the infimum because all quotients are positive.

For nonconstant a and strictly positive m, 2c min a<V_μ(θ)<2c max a. Changing m changes H in general, while the singularity extrema remain density independent. Direct differentiation gives H_s′=∫bm/a_s² and (√V_s)′=−[d+(V_s/2)H_s′]/(√V_s H_s), exactly the pairing with the displayed minimizing test. Uniform positivity on compact subsegments justifies differentiation and integration. Signed subtraction data give a signed identity. This is an actual relation among the declared moving data and the fixed-density cost; it does not differentiate the upper singularity volume.

D. The logarithmic endpoint calculation is correct. The height distribution is dτ/2, yielding H_s=(1/2)log((3−s)/(1−s)), V_s=4/log((3−s)/(1−s)), and the stated extrema. Differentiating √V_s gives the displayed derivative. Its nonnegative improper subtraction cost integrates to 2/√log3. Meanwhile σ_+(s) tends to 4. The raw zero-potential mass 4 is correctly distinguished from the type extrema and V_μ.

The endpoint is smooth semipositive and nef by its positive approximations. Its all-test infimum is zero by nonnegativity and comparison with the positive segment. A hypothetical strict current can be averaged over the second sphere, producing a genuine base potential while preserving a strict lower bound. Its vertical coefficient would require 1+τ≥ε almost everywhere, contradicted on an open neighborhood of the zero fiber. Thus the endpoint is nonbig. The argument proves a specific finite limiting cost; it establishes no general extension through big nef endpoints.

The separate first-moment threshold is also exact. Angular integration gives w=e^(−T)dT and dG_p∧d^cG_p=(1−e^(−T))dT. The positive moment tail is proportional to T^(2α−2)dT. It is finite exactly for α<1/2, logarithmically divergent at equality, and divergent by a power above it. The historical finite-energy proof is sound in its original α<1/2 range: full reference mass and finite first moment give finite closed energy; ordinary lower comparison and normalization give finite energy for v and v/2. Their full square masses determine the mixed trace and eliminate polar trace. The enlarged proof does not extend that energy argument beyond its valid range.

E. Gauge and pure-pullback laws are valid with the stated scope. Smooth gauges pair θ+dd^cf with v−f, preserving currents, actual measures, competitors, and extrema. Gauduchon numerators are unchanged by Stokes, including parameter-dependent gauge terms.

For a modification, properness supplies the local upper bound needed for canonical descent. Adding a dominating local quadratic, applying removal, and separating the coefficient measures on the analytic center retains the sharper nonclosed inequality. The converse pullback inequality follows from decreasing local psh regularization and preservation of the smooth lower bound. Almost-everywhere equality determines genuine representatives and extends ordinary inequalities. Biholomorphic locality and zero product mass on analytic sets then prove the actual pushforward identity, including when total mass is infinite. The supporting canonical results match [Demailly, Chapter I](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf).

The exceptional-curvature proof has the correct sign and valid Schur-complement bounds: first shrinking the fixed neighborhood, then choosing the parameter small, controls the errors. The normal-bundle identification follows from the blowup chart transitions, and the displayed Poincaré–Lelong potential produces an actual strict current upstairs. The independent cutoff-log construction also works. These witnesses acquire exceptional poles. A mutually equivalent witness at a blowup center away from D would be bounded near E; canonical restriction would give a strictly positive Hessian on E, contradicting Stokes. Consequently mass preservation and loss of mutual-type strictness coexist. No equality is claimed for exceptional-curvature subtraction or arbitrary smooth upstairs densities.

The remaining S11 support claims also check. Canonical divisorial removal gives the positive residual background with coefficient k=c−b. Averaging excludes k<0, while k=0 forces a constant residual average and contradicts its pole. For k>0 the small-curvature reference gives strict admissibility, and the same rough mass proof gives 2k min a and 2k max a. The original-background affine correction follows from ∫G_p dd^ca=a(p)−∫aw.

For the actual product embedding, a germ of transverse order j has radial integral ∫exp(−(j+1−sb)T+sT^α)dT. Its precise condition is j+1>sb, including divergence at equality. Hence the ideal coefficient is floor(sb) at every weight. Restriction of these invertible ambient ideals and total transform give the stated orders on every modification. This is not multiplier-ideal pullback commutation. The numerical examples, moment constants, strict witnesses, and residual variational values in n4–n7 follow from these calculations. The supplied support graph is acyclic, and every substantive dependency was checked; unnecessary graph edges are harmless.

Finiteness distinctions are retained. The construction proves finite positive mass over its particular entire ordinary types, including infinite first moments. It does not identify this with a general BMP assumption or infer positive lower mass from BMP. The auxiliary Kähler form supplies a bounded-mass reference with positive lower mass by bounded-product Stokes. Existing ordinary-type volume definitions and divisor/modification laws retain [BGL’s attribution](https://d-nb.info/1374372846/34), under its bounded-mass hypotheses. The direct formulas here have separate proofs.

Harmless wording corrections: claims that comparison or removal is expressly permitted must refer to the former S11 assignment, not this task; logarithmic moment divergence refers to the T cutoff; and signed moving data yield a signed subtraction identity. No substantial repair of the scoped proofs was necessary. The nonanalytic imposed type, rough optimization, infinite-moment range, and logarithmic nonclosed degeneration provide a nonvacuous example beyond a finite-divisor polynomial alone. Nevertheless, they supply neither an unrestricted moving-product construction nor the general geometric endpoint bridge, so unrestricted S18 completion remains unestablished.

passages.statement: For locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions φ₁,…,φ_p on a complex manifold of dimension n, with 1≤p≤n, their Bedford–Taylor product is a well-defined closed positive (p,p)-current, is symmetric and multilinear, is invariant under biholomorphic coordinate changes, and converges weakly under decreasing sequences with locally bounded limits. Its trace measures against smooth forms put no mass on pluripolar sets.

passages.statement: A genuine plurisubharmonic function that is not identically −∞ on any connected component is locally integrable and has positive distributional complex Hessian. Conversely, a distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable genuine plurisubharmonic representative. Radial smoothing converges decreasingly to that representative, and holomorphic pullbacks are plurisubharmonic, possibly identically −∞. Genuine plurisubharmonic representatives are determined by their almost-everywhere values.
passages.quote: there exists a unique function u ∈ Psh(Ω)

If A is a closed pluripolar subset of a complex manifold X and v is plurisubharmonic on X\A and locally bounded above near A, then v extends uniquely to a genuine canonical plurisubharmonic function on X.

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler manifold of dimension n, the non-pluripolar product of p closed positive (1,1)-currents, for 1≤p≤n, is well defined, has finite mass, is closed and positive, and puts no mass on pluripolar sets. Locally, ⟨dd^cφ⟩=1_{φ>−∞}dd^cφ. When the potentials are locally bounded outside a closed locally complete pluripolar set, the product is the trivial extension of the bounded Bedford–Taylor product from its complement.

On a compact Kähler manifold, let T₁,…,T_p and T₁′,…,T_p′ be tuples of closed positive (1,1)-currents, with corresponding currents cohomologous and all potentials having small unbounded locus, meaning local boundedness outside a closed locally complete pluripolar set. If every T_j is less singular than T_j′ in ordinary bounded order, then {⟨T₁∧⋯∧T_p⟩}−{⟨T₁′∧⋯∧T_p′⟩} is pseudoeffective.

For a closed strictly positive Kähler background K on a compact Kähler manifold, finite Aubin–Mabuchi energy is preserved by adding finite constants and making a potential less singular, and implies full non-pluripolar top mass. For a full-mass K-psh potential φ normalized by φ≤0, finite Aubin–Mabuchi energy is equivalent to ∫(−φ)⟨(K+dd^cφ)^n⟩<∞.

On a compact complex manifold with the bounded mass property, the lower and upper volumes of a quasi-closed positive (1,1)-current T are respectively the infimum and supremum of non-pluripolar top masses over positive currents in its dd^c-class with equivalent ordinary singularities, and both are finite. Adding an effective real divisor preserves both volumes, and pullback by a proper modification between smooth compact complex manifolds preserves both volumes.
